Do you even know what you’re saying? 
You made a fatal mistake. A trained rescuer should know that every second counts during cardiac arrest from drowning. Chest compressions and rescue breathing should not have been stopped while Rene and Divine were being carried to the ambulance or during transport to the hospital. CPR is performed to maintain blood flow and oxygen to the brain and vital organs until a pulse returns or advanced medical care takes over. Did you believe that waiting until arrival at the hospital to restart CPR would save them? By then, precious minutes had already been lost. When someone is in cardiac arrest, interruptions in CPR can significantly reduce the chances of survival. If CPR was stopped during transport, the likelihood of arriving at the hospital with any chance of recovery would have been greatly diminished. By the time you reached them to the hospital without continuous resuscitation efforts, you made this situation to be “death on arrival”.  Please re-educate yourself and the team so this mistake will not repeat again. 

May the soul of Rene and Adili rest in peace. Lord, I pray to comfort both families and give them strength during this difficult time as both families is grieving on the loss of their beloved Rene and Adili. Amen 🙏

The caveat of BLS is it should be started immediately upon seeing the patient. 

No pulse —> Start CPR right away and check for a pulse every 2 mins.
Pulse present but not breathing —> Give rescue breaths only; CPR is not needed.

The brain can start to suffer permanent damage after about 4–6 minutes without enough oxygen. Waiting to transport a patient to a hospital 10 minutes away without providing CPR or rescue breaths can greatly reduce their chances of survival and recovery.

Doing something immediately is far better than doing nothing while waiting for transport.

Paulit ulit na line during BLS - "The scene is safe, I am safe. Check responsiveness. Check for pulse & breathing. No pulse, no breathing. START CPR. text:
Alam nyo bakit nakaka trigger yung statement nya? Kasi if she had in fact undergone proper BLS training, she should have been familiar with the sequence ng BLS & the consequence of stopping the CPR. 

Anteee tinuro po sa BLS about Chest Compression Fraction (CCF) which is the amount of time spent giving high quality CPR. And this CCF plays a big role in the survival of the patient. High CCF = Better chances of survival. Low CCF = Poorer chances of survival. At ano ba yung most common reason na mababa yung CCF? Long interruptions in between CPR. 

Kaya nga kahit during rhythm check, when we check if may pulse & spontaneous breathing na, it is recommended sa AHA guideline ng BLS to limit this interruption to not more than 10 seconds. You read that right, NOT MORE THAN 10 SECONDS. 

Pero makikita nyo sa drone video na nung pina hinto nya yung pag CPR, parang naglakas pa sila ng ilang minute para malipat sa transport vehicle. Kahit oa sabihin niyang malapit lang yung ambulance but based sa video it took more than 10 seconds. So yung pasyente pa yung nag adjust na mailapit sya sa transport vehicle para mabigyan daw ng paunang lunas which is CPR na pina tigil nung emergency responder. 🙄 Or kung hindi kayang ilapit yung ambulance, wala palang wheeled stretcher yung ambulance nila para yung yung dalhin papunta sa patient? Or kung wala talaga, then atleast nag bigay sya ng continuous CPR kahit nung naglalakad pa lng sila.

text:
I'm not saying she was entirely at fault for the death of the two young men, but an irresponsible Coach + an ill-equipped establishment + a poor emergency response is apparently a very deadly combo.

I grieve with the families of these two young men, as their deaths may have been preventable. 

May this become a lesson for all healthcare providers including first responders and to anyone involved in emergency care to take BLS training seriously. When you attend a BLS course, don't treat it as just another certification or just for the CPD units. Learn the principles, understand the rationale behind them, and practice the skills until you become confident with them. 

Every action taken, or apparently not taken during those critical first minutes at the shoreline can mean the difference between life and death. That is why proper training, sound judgment, and adherence to established resuscitation guidelines are so important.

Hindi na natin mababago yung mga nangyari. But may this tragedy be a wake-up call to everyone and encourage better training, better preparedness, and better emergency response systems. The goal of BLS is not merely to perform CPR, and the goal of first responders is not simply to transport patients to the nearest hospital as quickly as possible, but to give every patient the best possible chance of survival.
